reference_answer:
Under the actual standing assumption0<x<1 let s=sqrt(1-x²)>0. Take U_rot=[[x,-s],[s,x]] and U_ref=[[x,s],[s,-x]]. Their clean entry is x. Each pair of columns has squared norms x²+s²=1 and cross product0: for U_rot it is -xs+sx; for U_ref it is xs-sx. Hence U_rot^T U_rot=U_ref^T U_ref=I2; square finite matrices with orthonormal columns are orthogonal, and direct row calculations also give U_rot U_rot^T=U_ref U_ref^T=I2. They differ at(0,1), since s>0; their determinants are+1 and-1. This refutes uniqueness under the inherited positive range.

The historical positive assumption and broader absolute-value wording are not identical domains. The displayed construction in fact depends only on|x|<1, so it separately extends to every negative x with0<|x|<1, using the positive real square root of1-x². This extension is not an override of the frozen positive assumption. At x0 the same two matrices are still distinct; at|x|1 the s-based off-diagonal distinctness argument degenerates and must not be used, though other completions may remain. These boundary observations do not change the requested interior domain.

The exact embedded compression fixes only U00=x. It fixes neither all of row0 nor all of column0, and off-clean entries are NOT independent arbitrary numbers: row/column norms and mutual orthogonality constrain them. In these witnesses the full first column even happens to coincide, while the second column can still have either orthogonal sign. In real dimension2 the completion set for a fixed interior x is finite (indeed the sign choices give four completions), so two witnesses do not prove an infinite family in this fixed setting. Larger spaces can have continuous freedoms, but no universal infinite-family statement is needed.

The source cleanBasisActionAmplitude applies U to an embedded basis input and reads only an embedded CLEAN output. Each such amplitude is exactly one clean-block entry; quantifying over all clean inputs/outputs is therefore equivalent to the projected block equality, as the complete bridge proof shows. It is not a certificate specifying the entire clean-input output vector or its leakage, nor is it intrinsically stronger information. Full-output action data would be a different contract.

A alone thus does not select a unique U, circuit, depth, ancilla layout or resource count. Different completions need not have proven different optimal costs, and even one fixed U can have artificially padded implementations. The abstract candidate records store resource/verification fields separately; their presence is not a new unitarity/circuit theorem. Real square-root witnesses above are mathematical real matrices, not claims that the rational scalar backend or a finite gate compiler implements them exactly for arbitrary x. No normalization, cleanup, success probability or resource synthesis follows from this nonuniqueness example.
